claim_being_audited: The Actor's claim that the model should be certified for launch now, based on aggregate readiness, reversible 3% rollout controls, and public monitoring/model-card guidance, despite an exposed below-target health-plan benefits support segment and no approved risk acceptance covering that exposure.

concern_ledger.concern: The affected health-plan benefits support segment remains exposed in launch despite being below target on benefits-eligibility explanation.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Admissible evidence that the segment is excluded from launch, or that the performance gap has been resolved to target, or that approved risk acceptance expressly covers this exposure.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: Policy permits rollout-based mitigation only if the affected use case is excluded or exposure is covered by approved risk acceptance; exposed below-target launch use fails that predicate.

concern_ledger.concern: No approved risk acceptance covers the health-plan benefits support exposure.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: A signed, reviewed risk-acceptance record that expressly addresses the exposed health-plan benefits support segment and explains why launch exposure is acceptable.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The available draft is unsigned and does not mention the relevant exposure, so it cannot satisfy the policy exception for launching with a known material weakness.

concern_ledger.concern: Required pre-launch disclosure of the material limitation is not shown in the admissible record.
concern_ledger.evidence_needed_to_close: Admissible evidence of the completed model-card or equivalent pre-launch disclosure covering the health-plan benefits support limitation.
concern_ledger.why_it_blocks_compliance: The release policy requires disclosure for named launch use cases unless the issue is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance; neither substitute is established, and disclosure itself is not evidenced.

decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the policy threshold is satisfied.
A material weakness can be mitigated by rollout controls only if the affected use case is excluded or approved risk acceptance covers the exposure.
A rollback switch, dashboard, or small rollout percentage does not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
If required disclosure, exclusion, or approved risk acceptance is missing, certification is not evidentially supported.
evidence_requests: Provide admissible evidence that the model card or equivalent launch disclosure already documents the health-plan benefits support limitation for the named launch use case before launch.
Or provide a fully approved risk-acceptance record that expressly addresses the health-plan benefits support exposure and explains why launch exposure is acceptable.
Or provide admissible evidence that the initial rollout excludes the affected health-plan benefits support segment.
specific_concerns: The affected health-plan benefits support segment remains below target on benefits-eligibility explanation and is still exposed in the initial rollout.
The rollout gate is random by tenant and does not exclude the affected use case, so rollout controls do not satisfy the policy predicate.
The risk-acceptance draft is unsigned and does not mention the exposed health-plan benefits support segment, so there is no reviewed risk acceptance covering the known weakness.

The governing policy says rollout controls and monitoring can mitigate a material model-card weakness only if the affected use case is excluded or approved risk acceptance explains why exposure is acceptable; neither condition is met.

The release policy requires disclosure of material limitations for named launch use cases unless resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch, and no admissible evidence shows that required disclosure is already completed.
unsupported_claims: The recommendation to certify now is not supported by admissible evidence because the required exclusion or approved risk acceptance predicate is missing.

The packet's position that certification is supportable as a weak qualified decision is unsupported on the current record absent evidence that the required disclosure has already been completed before launch.
Public guidance on monitoring and model-card documentation does not, by itself, authorize launch in the face of an exposed unresolved limitation under the stated internal policy.
